ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the side length of square $ABCD$ is 4. Point $E$ is a moving point on line segment $BC$. Connect $AE$, and rotate $AE$ clockwise by $90^\circ$ around point $E$ to $EF$. Connect $BF$, and take the midpoint $M$ of $BF$. If point $E$ moves from point $B$ to point $C$, what is the length of the path traveled by point $M$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Because rotating line AE clockwise by $90^\circ$ around point E brings it to line EF,\\
therefore EF$\perp$AE.\\
When point E is located at point B, point M is at the midpoint G of BC,\\
when point E is at point C, point M is at the midpoint H of CD, the path traveled by point M is the length of GH\\
Because the side length of square ABCD is 4,\\
therefore $GH=2\sqrt{2}$,\\
thus, the length of the path traveled by point M is $\boxed{2\sqrt{2}}$.

Because E moves linearly along BC and the rotation operation is rigid and fixed by 90°, F moves linearly along that segment. Now M is the midpoint of BF, with B fixed, so the locus of M is the image of the F-locus under a homothety centered at B with scale 1/2.
